what's a heap
A heap is a complete binary tree stored in a list. In a min-heap the smallest item is at index 0.
and heappush?
It adds the item at the end and sifts it up: O(log n).
heappop?
It removes the root, moves the last item to the top and sifts it down: O(log n).
why log n
Because the tree's height is about log2(n), and an item moves at most one level per swap.
ok what is heapify
It turns a whole list into a heap in O(n) by sifting down from the last parent.
why not n log n
Most nodes are near the bottom and only move a little, so the total is about 2n swaps.
can heap do max
Python's heapq is a min-heap. Push -x to simulate a max-heap.
top k largest?
Keep a min-heap of size k; pop whenever it grows past k. That's O(n log k).
is heap sorted
No. Only the parent-child order holds; the list as a whole isn't sorted.
heap[1] is second smallest?
Not always. The second smallest is one of the root's children: heap[1] or heap[2].
